plain.en: a program that learned from many examples

means.en: A model is a program whose behaviour comes from numbers that were set by training. In this course a model reads text or pictures and gives back a guess or a new piece of text or picture.

plain.en: a list of exact instructions

means.en: A program is a list of exact instructions that a computer follows one line at a time. A computer cannot guess what you meant.

plain.en: the one starting number for random choices

means.en: A computer makes random numbers from one starting number, called the seed. The same seed gives the same starting noise, so you can repeat a run.

plain.en: a program that makes pictures from words

means.en: Stable Diffusion is a real picture-making model. It starts from noise and removes the noise step by step until a picture is left.

plain.en: making a picture by removing noise step by step

means.en: Diffusion is the method of making a picture from noise, one small step at a time. It is named after the way a drop of ink spreads through water.

plain.en: a piece of text that the model reads

means.en: A token is a piece of text, and it need not mean anything. Every model cuts text into tokens before it does anything else.

plain.en: a token's number in the token list

means.en: A computer needs numbers, so each token is swapped for a number called its token id. The id only says which token it is. It says nothing about the token's meaning.

plain.en: the fixed list of all tokens a model knows

means.en: The token list holds every token the model can read or write. A token's place in this list is its token id.

plain.en: the long practice in which a model's settings are nudged

means.en: In training, a model guesses, checks the guess against the real answer, and gets its settings nudged to do better. When training is finished the settings stop changing.

plain.en: the large collection of text a model practises on

means.en: The pile of text that a model practises on is called the training data. A model can only learn what the pile shows it, so a pile that leans one way makes the answers lean that way.

plain.en: the numbers inside a model that training changes

means.en: A model's settings are the numbers that decide its scores. Real models have billions of them.

plain.en: a small change to a setting

means.en: A nudge is a small change to a setting that makes the next guess a little less wrong. Many nudges, one after another, are how a model learns.

plain.en: one number for how bad a guess was

means.en: Wrongness is a single number that tells how far a guess is from the right answer. Training tries to make it smaller.

plain.en: a number a model gives each choice

means.en: The model gives every possible next word a number called a score. A high score means the token is likely, and the highest score is its guess.

plain.en: a small model we built to show one idea

means.en: A Toy is a small, simplified model that we made for this course. Its numbers are set by hand to show what a real model tends to do, not what it does exactly.

plain.en: learning one case exactly and nothing more

means.en: Memorising a line looks perfect on that line but fails on a new one. Good learning keeps what many examples share.

plain.en: a word's list of numbers

means.en: An embedding is a list of numbers that training gives to a token. Tokens used in similar sentences get similar lists. It is a record of the text, not of the world.

plain.en: a number that says how alike two lists are

means.en: Closeness compares two lists of numbers. Its top value is 1, and a higher number means the lists are more alike.

plain.en: taking numbers from the other words in the sentence

means.en: In attention, each word in a sentence gives a share of its numbers to a word, so that the word gets a working copy that fits this sentence.

plain.en: a word's numbers mixed with shares from its neighbours

means.en: A working copy is a mix: each word's numbers times its share, all added together. A new sentence needs a new working copy.

plain.en: answers that lean one way because the pile leans

means.en: When results lean one way because of what the training data holds, we call that bias. It can happen even when no line in the pile is false.

plain.en: a run option that makes picking more or less adventurous

means.en: Temperature is a run option for the picking step. A low temperature picks the likely tokens, and a high one lets less likely tokens in. Training does not change it.

plain.en: everything a model can read at one moment

means.en: The context window holds the request and the reply so far. The model can use only the text that is in it.

plain.en: a confident answer that is made up

means.en: A hallucination is a confident, made-up answer. It comes from the normal writing loop picking likely tokens, not from a broken part.

plain.en: a program with an answer key

means.en: A checker is a program that compares an answer with an answer key. The model alone cannot be sure its own answer is right.

plain.en: a language for writing programs

means.en: Python is a language for writing programs. Its lines are exact, and a computer runs them one at a time.

plain.en: a named box that holds a value

means.en: A variable is a named box that holds a value. A program can read the box and change what it holds.

plain.en: the ordinary computer that runs a program

means.en: The runner is an ordinary computer that runs the program the model wrote. It is separate from the model, and it is what finds out what happens.

plain.en: a mistake in a program

means.en: A bug is a mistake in a program. A program with a bug may still run and give a wrong answer.

plain.en: one small square of colour

means.en: A pixel is one small square of colour in a picture. Each pixel is stored as numbers, so a picture is a long list of numbers.

plain.en: hidden

means.en: Latent numbers are numbers that you do not see in a picture but that control it. Latent simply means hidden.

plain.en: a part that squeezes a picture into a short list of numbers

means.en: An encoder reads a picture and writes down its latent numbers. It makes a long list of pixel numbers into a short one.

plain.en: a part that opens latent numbers out into a picture

means.en: A decoder takes latent numbers and opens them out into the full picture. It draws the pixels again from the short list.

plain.en: a picture held in a short list of numbers

means.en: A latent code is a picture held in a list of numbers that is much smaller than the picture. A decoder turns it back into pixels.

plain.en: all the latent codes that could exist

means.en: Latent space is all the latent codes that could exist, taken together. Almost every code in it makes no sensible picture.

plain.en: random numbers added to a picture's numbers

means.en: Noise is random numbers added to a picture's numbers. With enough noise, no picture can be seen.

plain.en: taking noise away

means.en: Denoising is taking noise away from a picture. A model does it in many small steps.

plain.en: the model's estimate of the noise that was added

means.en: The model is asked to estimate the random numbers that were added to a picture. This estimate is called the noise guess, and taking it away leaves a cleaner picture.

plain.en: the journey from noise to picture

means.en: Walking back is the journey from pure noise to a picture. Each step removes a small part of the noise.

plain.en: how far the guidance pushes the picture

means.en: Strength is the amount by which the words push a picture away from the guess without words. A bigger strength follows the prompt more closely.

plain.en: the words you give a model

means.en: A prompt is the text you give a model to start from. The model uses it to pick what comes next.

plain.en: an extra part that rewrites your words

means.en: A prompt expander is an extra part that adds detail to your short words before the picture model sees them.

plain.en: a made picture, video or voice of a real person

means.en: A deepfake is a made picture, video or voice showing a real person doing or saying what they never did.
